title: Create human-oriented documentation navigation
status_detail: The human response `accept` accepted the completed implementation. Accepted result: docs/index.rst is the sole root landing page after the accepted inventory's docs/index.md merge disposition; every maintained first-level docs section has an index; visible root navigation covers user, scientific, software, verification, project-record, and history entry points; and Sphinx collection adds the new section indexes without collecting detailed repository-first computational, research, publication, proof, or meeting records. Sphinx HTML and linkcheck builds with warnings as errors, first-level index and root-reachability checks, retained-link checks, Harness projection verification, repository Harness validation, and git diff validation pass. Harness synchronization was required only for managed Task lifecycle updates, not for the navigation-only documentation result. No successor is activated and automatic successor activation remains disabled.
objective: Provide one obvious documentation landing page and index-driven navigation for every first-level maintained section.
authorized_scope: Create or revise the root landing page around human tasks: start here, architecture, user guide, concepts, computational work, research, API reference, verification, development, publications, and history.
Add an index.md or index.rst to every first-level maintained documentation section and make explicit navigation the primary discovery mechanism.
Simplify Sphinx collection and hidden navigation without broadening publication scope for restricted or intentionally uncollected records.
completion_criteria: A reader can reach every current first-level documentation section from the root page without knowing repository-specific numeric filenames.
Every first-level maintained section has an index, no current page relies solely on hidden toctree discovery, and all maintained links resolve.
Sphinx passes with warnings as errors and no harness synchronization is needed for the navigation-only result.
exclusions: Do not perform bulk filename normalization, rewrite scientific or publication content, expose private material, or activate a successor automatically.
Do not retain duplicate root pages with conflicting navigation authority.
